content:
alex: Heads-up — we've seen a spike of Xid 13 / ECC events on us-west-2 GPU fleet over the last 48h. Need faster evidence collection so we can triage flaky cards faster.

maya: Ugh. Do we have samples? Are these tied to specific driver versions or instance types?

alex: Short sample from node gpu-uw2-17 this morning — dmesg snippet and nvidia-smi at time of error:

alex: ```
[Mon Oct 27 07:12:03] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[Mon Oct 27 07:12:03] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.

$ nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
Product Name : NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
Driver Version : 535.54.03
...
GPU 0: ECC errors corrected: 12  (page, device)
```

lee: Ok. We desperately need a reliable ingest for dmesg + journalctl + nvidia-smi when a GPU reports Xid or ECC > threshold. Right now traces are scattered across instances and it's manual.

sam: Proposal: add an on-host hook (systemd service) that watches kernel messages and nvidia-smi outputs and pushes a single structured JSON blob to our logs when an actionable error appears (Xid, ECC count jump, thermal/power warnings).

maya: What triggers do we want? Xid codes are noisy. Maybe thresholds: any Xid 13/31, or delta ECC > 5 within 5 min, or GPU offline.

alex: Yes. Trigger list I'd start with: Xid 13, Xid 31, GPU fell off the bus, ECC corrected delta >= 5 in 5m, local driver panic, and nv-hostengine resets.

lee: Suggested capture fields for the blob: host, gpu_index, pci_addr, driver_version, kernel_version, uptime, last_100_dmesg_lines_matching("NVRM|Xid|GPU"), nvidia-smi -q snapshot, journalctl -k -n 200, time window. Also attach a SHA256 of the full raw payload.

sam: Implementation sketch: systemd unit `gpu-loghook.service` + small binary `gpu-loghook` that: (1) listens to /dev/kmsg or dbus for kernel events, (2) on trigger runs:
```
journalctl -k -b -1 --no-pager | tail -n 200 | grep -i -E "NVRM|Xid|GPU" > /tmp/gpu-dmesg-snippet.txt
nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(hostname)-gpu${GPU}.xml
dmesg -T | tail -n 200 >> /tmp/gpu-dmesg.txt
```
then POSTs structured JSON to our logs endpoint (Loki/OpenSearch) with tags `region`, `instance_type`, `device_model`, `driver_version`.

maya: For privacy/compliance: make sure we scrub user-level PII — but machine logs shouldn't have it. Also keep payload size bounded (truncate >100KB).

alex: Parsing rules idea: map Xid codes to likely root causes with confidence: 13 -> link/PCI/firmware / sometimes TLB; 31 -> ECC/thermal; 43 -> SMI reset — we can auto-suggest drain+replace if Xid 13 repeats 3 times in 24h.

lee: We should add a short regex set for quick classification so on-call gets immediate hint in alert: e.g., `Xid \(([A-Za-z0-9:]+)\): (\d+)` and `ECC.*corrected.*(\d+)`.

infra-oncall: +1 to auto-classification. Can we also include a small `--collect` API to attach to existing incident runbook so the agent can be kicked manually from PagerDuty?

sam: Yep — expose a simple POST to instance agent that triggers immediate collection for a given gpu_index. Handy for postmortem repro.

ops-bot: Notice: node gpu-uw2-17 is currently cordoned by infra-oncall and a drain is in progress (:information_source:). Ticket #INF-7182 linked.

maya: Thoughts on backend: Loki is good for raw logs + labels, OpenSearch for full-text searches, but we want a single quick dashboard for GPU health. Maybe store the structured blobs in a dedicated index and keep raw artifacts in object storage with the blob pointing to the S3 key.

alex: Agreed. Index blob in OpenSearch with `s3_uri` pointing to full payload. Alert rule: when a host emits >=2 Xid13 blobs within 6h -> auto-create ticket + annotate host for replacement candidate.

lee: One more operational nit: make sure to record pci topology (root complex) and host BIOS/fac firmware versions in the blob. We've seen vendor BIOS fixes that fixed fall-off-the-bus.

maya: I'll prototype the systemd hook + small parser this week. Sam/lee can help with the alert mapping and infra-oncall can test on the cordoned node.

alex: Thanks — this should cut triage time dramatically. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Action: created task `infra/gpu-loghook` -> assignees: maya, lee, sam. Due: 2025-11-05.
